- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- Forecasting horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing downward momentum; adjust for mean reversion by adding 1–2% downward bias in mid-to-late period.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits overconfidence; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid over-optimism.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above true) are common; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x recent high or 1.2x 30d moving average.
- If true outcome shows sharp decline after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add 3–5% downward bias in 10–15 day horizon if sentiment remains neutral.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility into future; if 30d history shows high variance, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to prevent overfitting.
